OriginalChannelInformation.original_text: All sound files have an equal small chance to play. However, they can only play if they are within their

dedicated activity ranges AND channel.There are 7 main channels, with channel 0 being reserved for more special cases. Some sound files interact with voice commands or simply just to noise input from the microphone.
The general structure to maintain thematic cohesion:
Channel 1 is meant for very small strange sound oddities. Not much interactivity, just short strange sounds.
Channel 2 is a more intense version of channel 1. This channel is for longer, more coherent sounds and words. Meant to be a bit more curious.
Channel 3 is reserved for more musical anomalies. Anything regaurded as cursed or haunted music should be in this channel. Whispers and other mantra like sounds can be found here too.
Channel 4 is a more interactive layer where using the mic can produce a lot of output. This channel represents talking to spirits just like in those cheesy tv shows.
Channel 5 will contain more monstrous and horrifying sounds. Most all monster and creature sounds will be in this channel.
Channel 6 has a demonic theme. The most evil and creepy sentences and sound effects are here. This channel is very interactive with voice.
Channel 7 is meant for very special and unique cases. Most likely will be used for planned events. The strongest entities are planned for this
channel.
Each channel changes the background static very subtly so that each has its own distinct tone:
Channel 0: Default
Channel 1: Default
Channel 2: Slightly higher pitched
Channel 3: Slightly lower pitched
Channel 4: Less scratchy White Noise
Channel 5: Brown Noise
Channel 6: Lower, almost monotonous tones
Channel 7: Quiet static

EventBuilderGuide.instructions: Define new conversations and interactive events using generic event IDs, states, rules, response pools, and action sequences.
Configuration blueprint for the future event engine. A Pi loader and the listed trigger/action handlers still need implementation.
1.0. Read named Excel tables. Field names are stable IDs, native numbers, booleans, and enums. Guide and Dictionary are documentation.
Preserves 60% opening, equal 25% answers, forced yes keywords, goodbye hangup, and silence greater than 6 seconds.
On channel 5 at Activity 80–100, creation has one 20% response roll. One of four equal-weight sounds plays on success.
your_event is disabled and assigned to channels 4 and 6. Copy its rows across the data tabs and replace its IDs and keyword.
sword_example is disabled. It needs the active sword Program and PKE mode. SCAN at Activity 98–100 unlocks haunted_sword once.
Copy an Events row, give it a unique event_id and name, and keep enabled=FALSE while editing its related tables.
Add States rows for that event. initial_state must exist. Reuse names such as idle and contact independently across events.
For Radio events, add every allowed channel in EventChannels. Multiple rows mean multiple allowed channels. PKE events ignore channels.
Add Rules for the event: state, trigger, keyword group, activity range, chance, action set, and next states.
Define Actions and any Keywords or Responses referenced by the rules. Keep action steps unique and consecutive from 1.
Add new audio files and definitions to the radio sound catalog. Sound References lists IDs used here; it does not duplicate playback settings.
Replace placeholder assets/keywords, verify referenced states and actions, assign channels, then set Events.enabled=TRUE.
Filter event mode, Program, channels, state, trigger, activity, cooldown and use limit. Then evaluate event priority followed by rule priority.
For one input, consider events and rules in ascending priority order. Ties use event_id then rule_id. Default consume_input=TRUE prevents a second reaction.
Roll once for a matching rule. On failure use on_failure_state and consume the input if configured. Do not roll once per response sound.
play_pool chooses one eligible sound by weight. Base catalog enabled flag and activity bounds still apply. No eligible sound means action failure.
For play_sound and play_pool, channel eligibility is owned by EventChannels. Base SoundChannels continues to govern spontaneous ambient playback.
Complete the action set before on_success_state applies. Opening Ben audio must actually complete before his state becomes active.
Stop on a required action failure and use on_failure_state. Optional failed actions are skipped. Previously completed actions are not rolled back.
Rule chance × eligible pool share = overall sound chance. Creation gives 20% × 25% = 5% per sound when all four are eligible.
Idle time starts at state entry or completed response. Detected voice resets it when configured. Paused time does not count. Ben times out only above 6 s.
Emit one idle_timeout per timer expiry. Rearm after timer reset or state reentry. Required hangup failure can still close the event via failure state.
voice_input fires on push-to-talk release only when vocal input was detected. scan_press is SCAN in PKE mode. Radio SCAN records voice.
button_a_press and button_b_press identify the square buttons. scope_enter fires when an event becomes eligible. activity_enter fires on entering a rule range.
from_state=* matches any state in that event. next-state keep preserves current state. These markers are reserved and cannot be state IDs.
max_fires_session=0 means unlimited. Count successful action sets only. Cooldown starts after success. Both reset on event reset.
Every event stores its own state and rule counts. Session state clears on restart. Disk state survives restart until manual reset.
on_scope_exit resets when mode, Program, or allowed channel stops matching. Switching between two assigned channels keeps the same event state.
unlock_entry saves local progress and is idempotent. The scenario supplies the entry text and image. show_entry opens that entry after unlock.
The named triggers and action types define the planned engine contract. A capability outside these types needs an engine/schema extension.
Blank program_id means no scenario required. Blank keyword_group accepts any detected voice. Blank unused action arguments and timer settings stay unset.
Add rows inside the named tables. For new Response rows, copy the selection_probability formula down. More than 995 pool rows requires extending its range.
Ben/Creation follow the agreed radio configuration. Template timeouts, priorities, reset/storage policies and action examples are proposed editable defaults.
After integration, migrate Ben/Creation to this engine or disable their old VoiceRules. Do not activate two controllers for the same interaction.
Disable an event in Events to keep its definitions for later. Delete all linked rows only when you want to remove the event completely.

radio or pke. Controls whether Radio channel gating applies.

Starting state for this event. Must exist in EventStates.

on_scope_exit or manual_only. Affects state and successful-use counters.
session or disk. Disk state and counters persist locally, scoped by event_id.
One channel 0–7 per row. Multiple rows give one event access to multiple channels.

gt means strictly greater than. gte means greater than or equal to.

Required current state. * accepts any state within that event.
voice_input, idle_timeout, scan_press, button_a_press, button_b_press, scope_enter, activity_enter.
Lower rule priority wins within an event. Specific keyword rules should precede general voice rules.

Inclusive activity bounds, 0–100. Use 0 and 100 for all levels.
One response chance for the rule. 0.2 displays as 20%.
ID of a sequence in EventActions.
State after the action set finishes successfully.
State after probability failure or required action failure.
Minimum time after a successful action set before this rule can succeed again. 0 disables cooldown.
Maximum successful runs between resets. 0 means unlimited. Disk events persist this count.

Sequence ID and order, starting at 1. The pair must be unique.
play_sound, play_pool, display_message, set_screen_color, restore_screen_color, unlock_entry, show_entry, show_image, delay.

TRUE: failure stops the action set. FALSE: failure skips this action and continues.

Relative selection weight. Four weights of 1 give four equal 25% candidates.
